The next morning, before classes, Agnes met Theodore in her office wearing an emerald dress with a severe collar cut right up to the throat, from which straps fell to hold up her full, if tastefully moderate, breasts with their beauty marks. It also bared her firm shoulders and her womanly belly, beneath which the muscles played whenever Agnes laughed or drew on a cigarette. The magess loved both.

And Agnes happened to be doing both just then.

Together with the miniskirt, the bronze high-heeled shoes and the golden nails made of melted-down etons, Agnes's look defied every principle of the Academy, where students were obliged to wear clothes of regulation colors and cut, and where the Pigsty's drilling in high collars and robes was kept up by resident mages, graduates already, until grey hair and the grave. Agnes's green robe on the hanger behind her did nothing to mend matters: it was strewn with sequins that threw the morning sun back across the walls like an emerald disco ball.

But Agnes could afford to dress as brightly as any Volevich, because curators, who were appointed at the end of the fourth circle, held practically boundless power. Exams aside, it was the curators who decided whether a student was worthy of moving on to the fifth circle to pursue a magical specialization, and who steered a mage's path all the way to expulsion or graduation.

And there were a great, great many juicy rumors about how Agnes, in every way unworthy, had got this important curatorial post. A battle magess and a veteran, Agnes didn't even hold a diploma from the fifth circle, and rumor had it she hadn't served out her ten years as a battle magess either. The rumors about a three-day orgy in the rector's offices came in three versions. In two more, Senators and Minor Gods joined in. Anna knew every version, down to the smallest detail.
